snapshot.targets: Annual grasses and broadleaf weeds before germination. Examples below; the label has the complete species list.
snapshot.apply: Remove existing weeds. Spread evenly with a calibrated drop or rotary spreader around established, listed ornamentals. Water in with at least ½ inch within 24 hours.
rates: Chamberbitter, bittercress, spotted spurge, yellow woodsorrel.
limits: Does not control weeds already growing.
No annual bedding plants, unrooted cuttings, or groundcovers that are not established.
At 150 lb/acre or higher: wait at least 60 days between applications. Maximum 600 lb/acre in 12 months.
snapshot.name: Snapshot 2.5TG

f8012.targets: 8% nitrogen, 12% potash, 4% magnesium, 2% manganese. The nitrogen is slow release.
f8012.apply: Use a rotary or chest spreader, or spread by hand. Apply to dry foliage and water in soon afterward. Sweep granules off pavement.
rates: Up to four applications per year as needed.
Trees and larger shrubs: ½–1 lb / inch of trunk diameter
Distribute evenly from the outer foliage edge inward. Bag directions specify spring and late fall.
limits: Keep fertilizer out of water and storm drains.
Not for nursery container production.
f8012.program: Waves uses the canopy-width palm chart (width² ÷ 105, rounded down). That is a company rate choice; it is not the formula printed on this bag.
f8012.name: LESCO 8-0-12 #511542

f0016.targets: 16% potash, 6% magnesium, 2% manganese. Contains no nitrogen or phosphate.
f0016.apply: Use a rotary or chest spreader, or spread by hand. Apply to dry foliage and water in soon afterward. Sweep granules off pavement.
rates: Up to four applications per year as needed.
Trees and larger shrubs: ½–1 lb / inch of trunk diameter
Distribute evenly from the outer foliage edge inward. Bag directions specify spring and late fall.
limits: Keep fertilizer out of water and storm drains.
Not for nursery container production.
Harmful if inhaled; eye and skin irritant. Avoid breathing dust and wash after handling.
f0016.program: Waves uses the canopy-width palm chart (width² ÷ 105, rounded down). That is a company rate choice; it is not the formula printed on this bag.
f0016.name: LESCO 0-0-16 #510513

mnsulfate.targets: 29% manganese (water soluble). For manganese deficiency (frizzle-top) on palms: the newest fronds come out yellow, small, withered or frizzled. Common on queen, royal, pygmy date, paurotis and coconut palms. Contains no nitrogen or phosphate, so it is allowed during the June–September blackout.
mnsulfate.apply: Spread evenly under the canopy. No mixing or spraying. Keep granules off pavement, masonry and painted surfaces: manganese sulfate stains them. Old frizzled fronds will not recover; judge results on new fronds in 3–6 months.
rates: Small palms: ½–1 lb per palm
Large shrubs and trees: ¼–½ lb per plant
Landscape beds: ¼–½ lb / 100 sq ft
limits: Use only on a diagnosed deficiency (frizzle-top on new fronds); the routine palm fertilizer already carries 2% manganese.
Too much manganese can bring on iron deficiency; stay inside the label size class.
Stains masonry and painted surfaces; sweep and blow off hard surfaces.
May be harmful if swallowed; avoid breathing dust; wash after use.
mnsulfate.program: Manganese is a supplement on its own schedule, not one of the palm feedings counted by the three-month rule.
mnsulfate.source: Southern Agricultural Insecticides · SA-50 Manganese Sulfate bag label
mnsulfate.name: Manganese sulfate (Southern Ag)
mnsulfate.summary: lb per palm · label size class

mainspring.targets: Whiteflies, caterpillars, soft scales, leafminers, thrips, lace bugs, leaf-feeding beetles, and aphids on landscape ornamentals.
mainspring.apply: Spray for even, thorough foliage coverage when infestations are first detected. Do not make foliar applications during rain.
rates: Whiteflies, caterpillars, soft scales, and the other listed foliar pests except aphids.
limits: No application while bees forage or plants flower; wait until all petals have fallen.
At least 7 days between treatments. Outdoor maximum: 32 fl oz/acre/year, accounting for other cyantraniliprole products.
Keep people and pets out until sprays dry.
mainspring.program: The table retains the draft 4–8 fl oz/100 gal choice. Whether to use the full 2–8 range for whiteflies and caterpillars still needs your call.
mainspring.name: Mainspring GNL

distance.targets: Whiteflies and scale crawlers. Scale species include black, California red, euonymus, Florida wax, San Jose, and snow scale. Mealybugs: suppression only.
distance.apply: Cover all plant surfaces evenly to the point of runoff. The foliar table specifies 100 gal of mix per 20,000 sq ft. Time scale treatments for crawlers.
limits: Does not provide rapid adult-insect control.
Whitefly directions: second treatment in 14–28 days if needed; maximum two per six months or crop cycle.
Label advises against use on gardenia, schefflera, salvia, Boston fern, ghost plant, and coral bells. Test other plants first.
distance.name: Distance IGR

tristar.targets: Whiteflies, mealybugs, aphids and soft scales (Florida wax, cottony cushion). Use on live finds only, foliar only. Not for armored scale (euonymus, tea, false Florida red, oleander): use Distance, oil or a Zylam drench.
tristar.apply: Cover all plant surfaces evenly. The label sets the finished spray volume by plant size. Tank mixing with a surfactant may improve control of adult whiteflies; test a small area first. Allow 6 hours before overhead irrigation.
rates: Whiteflies, mealybugs, aphids and soft scales. Use the higher rate when pressure is high.
limits: Not for armored scale. Use Distance on crawlers, oil, or a Zylam drench.
Do not reapply more than once every 7 days.
Maximum 4 applications per calendar year; 25.3 fl oz per acre per application; 92.5 fl oz per acre per year.
Group 4A neonicotinoid: count it with Merit and Zylam in the annual 4A log.
Toxic to bees: do not apply while bees or other pollinators are actively visiting; dawn, dusk, or below 55°F lowers the risk.
Professional applicators only. Do not apply to bearing fruit trees.
tristar.name: TriStar 8.5 SL

tritek.targets: Listed aphids, leafminers, mites, plant bugs, psyllids, sawflies, scales, and whiteflies. Disease uses include black spot, powdery mildew, and rust.
tritek.apply: Add to water with agitation and keep agitating. Wet upper and lower leaf surfaces and the canopy evenly, without significant runoff.
rates: Landscape ornamentals, shade trees, and shrubs. The draft rows use 1% or 1.5% within this range.
limits: Live scale crawlers, nymphs, mites or sooty mold only. Not a routine spray.
Do not spray above 90°F.
Do not spray within 7 days of a forecast cold snap.
Do not treat moisture-stressed plants.
Check plant sensitivity before wide use.
Do not mix with NPK foliar fertilizer, sulfur, captan, carbaryl, or dimethoate; check the full incompatibility and timing directions.
Keep people and pets out until sprays dry.
tritek.name: TriTek 1%

floramite.targets: Listed spider mites and red mites, including two-spotted, southern red, citrus red, spruce spider, and bamboo spider mites.
floramite.apply: Spray both sides of leaves thoroughly when mites first appear. Use 1–4 qt of finished spray per 100 sq ft. Keep mix pH at 5.5–6.5.
rates: Lower rate for light populations or prevention; higher rate for heavier pressure or longer residual control.
limits: Not effective against broad, rust, or flat mites.
Maximum two applications per crop per year and 32 fl oz/acre/year.
Rotate after one application; use at least two alternative products before returning to Floramite.
floramite.source: Manufacturer specimen label · use rates pp. 6–8
floramite.name: Floramite SC

merit.equipmentNote: Measure finished solution in quarts or gallons. Calculate product dose from trunk diameter or shrub height.
merit.targets: Listed soft and armored scales, whiteflies, royal palm bug, and specified borers. Match the species to the label table.
merit.apply: Dose by tree trunk diameter measured 4½ ft above ground, or by shrub height. For soil injection, distribute at low pressure through at least four holes per plant; keep the area moist for 7–10 days.
rates: 0.1–0.2 fl oz / inch of trunk diameter or foot of shrub height
Soft scales, whiteflies, royal palm bug, and other pests in the first group.
Armored scales and specified borers. Trees ≥15 inches DBH have separate borer directions.
limits: Maximum 1.6 pt/acre/year.
Do not treat saturated soil or any Tilia species.
Follow the flowering and pollinator restrictions.
merit.program: Use the owned FlowZone soil injector kit with the 4-gal backpack. Tank capacity alone cannot determine the dose; plant measurements are required.
merit.name: Merit 2F

kphite.targets: Listed Phytophthora, Pythium, Rhizoctonia, Fusarium, and other ornamental diseases. Mildews have foliar directions.
kphite.apply: Use the directions for the plant and delivery method. Soil drench, foliar spray, and direct trunk injection are different label uses.
rates: The ornamental table also prints ⅛–¼ fl oz/gal.
Foliar: 1–2 qt in at least 100 gal / acre
The table also prints ⅓–⅔ fl oz/gal; see disease and plant directions.
limits: Do not treat dormant plants or plants under heat or moisture stress.
Do not apply less than 3 days apart.
Avoid conditions that keep tissue wet for more than 4 hours.
kphite.program: The FlowZone soil injector kit is available. Confirm the T&O container label and soil-delivery directions before setting an injector recipe. The old draft showed the foliar concentration beside root-rot treatment.
kphite.source: Plant Food Systems · EPA 73806-1 · T&O 0417 · p. 6
kphite.name: KPHITE 7LP

conserve.targets: Listed caterpillars, including bagworms, oleander caterpillars, Florida fern caterpillars, and fall webworms. Other target groups have different rates.
conserve.apply: Cover upper and lower leaf surfaces and penetrate dense foliage without excessive runoff. Treat bagworms while small and actively feeding; treat webworms before large webs form.
rates: 6 fl oz / 100 gal; 24 fl oz / acre.
Outdoor exposed thrips, leafminers, and mites use separate table entries.
limits: Do not treat flowering, pollen-shedding, or nectar-producing parts if bees may forage during the next 3 hours.
Use the resistance-management directions for the treatment site.
Keep people and pets out until sprays dry.
conserve.program: Replace the generic draft range with a target-specific recipe and a measurable batch size before implementation.
conserve.name: Conserve SC

dipel.targets: Young caterpillars that eat the leaves, including oleander caterpillar (oleander moth). Bt acts only on caterpillars, so it spares bees and the natural enemies that control scale and whitefly. Use on live finds only, while the caterpillars are small.
dipel.apply: Spray the leaves the caterpillars are eating, tops and undersides. On trees, mix by the 100-gallon rate; on shrubs and beds, weigh the product for the area treated so the per-acre rate is not exceeded. Caterpillars must eat the treated leaves; they stop feeding within an hour and die in 1–3 days. Repeat while young caterpillars are still feeding.
rates: Ornamental and shade trees (hydraulic sprayer). In a small sprayer: 1–2 tsp per gallon.
Shrubs, flowers, bedding plants and ornamentals: about 0.2–0.7 oz of product per 1,000 sq ft treated. Measure by area, not by gallons sprayed; use at least 50 gal of mix per acre.
limits: Repeat at the interval needed to keep control, usually every 3–14 days, depending on plant growth and the hatch.
Restricted-entry interval 4 hours.
Rain soon after spraying washes it off; plan for a dry window of 24–48 hours where possible.
Do not apply directly to water.
dipel.source: Valent BioSciences / Nufarm DiPel PRO DF · EPA 73049-39 · EPA-accepted label 2024-09-19
dipel.name: DiPel PRO DF
dipel.summary: Trees by tank · shrubs by area

zylam.targets: Listed soft and armored scales, whiteflies, mealybugs, lace bugs, and other ornamental insects. Aphids and certain thrips: suppression only.
zylam.apply: Spray for thorough coverage before populations build. The foliar guide uses 100 gal of mix per 20,000 sq ft. Drench and bark applications have separate instructions.
limits: No application while bees forage or plants flower; wait until all petals have fallen.
Foliar limit: 78.9 fl oz/acre/season; no more than three applications per growing season.
Follow Group 4A rotation restrictions and keep others out until dry.
zylam.name: Zylam Liquid
